title: Close the three maintainer-reported tenant defects: platform-only menus, empty tenant login audit, and plan differentiation owned by the frontend
goal: A manual acceptance pass found three user-visible defects: (1) a tenant administrator still sees platform-only console menus (tenant/menu/i18n management) and lands on a 403 page; (2) the tenant login-log page is empty because audit rows are written at platform scope; (3) every tenant plan exposes the same console surfaces because plan has no presentation-layer definition. This packet fixes all three at their real boundaries: one shared platform-surface classification consumed by menu reads, provisioning, role assignment, and permission caching; tenant attribution for login/security audit; and a frontend-owned plan registry that modules annotate, the shell filters, and the tenant form renders as a matrix. Backend role permissions remain the authorization boundary; the plan gate is UX-only and no plan-specific data is seeded.
findings: A1 (P1): tenant sessions receive platform-only menu rows. Provisioning copied the platform administrator's menu and permission bindings verbatim into each tenant namespace, so tenant_admin owned system.tenant, system:menu, and system:i18n grants; the navigation tree returned them unfiltered, and each page's route group answered 403 tenant.platformOnly. Reproduced via a tenant-admin login: sidebar showed the platform surfaces; direct navigation rendered the 403 page. Fixed by classifying the platform surfaces once in pkg/tenant, filtering tenant-scoped menu reads, dropping those bindings during provisioning, and rejecting them on tenant-owned role writes.

A2 (P2): existing tenants provisioned before the fix would keep the stale grants because re-provisioning only adds missing rows, and GetUserPerms could serve a cached permission list containing platform-only keys for up to five minutes. Fixed with an idempotent startup repair scoped to tenant_id <> 0, a user-ownership check before reusing a cached list, and a filtered write-back.

B1 (P1): tenant login logs and security events were written at platform scope (tenant_id 0) while tenant administrators read with WithTenantScope(tenant), so the audit page showed no rows. The login flow never used the resolved tenant claim for audit attribution; MFA verification also lost the challenge tenant on pre-session failures. Fixed by stamping successful rows with the issued tenant claim, failed attempts with the known subject's owning tenant, pinning the MFA request to the challenge tenant, and only falling back to the request context for events without a subject. Compat mode remains platform-global (0).

C1 (P1): plan tiers existed only as a tenants.plan string with no presentation-layer meaning, so free/basic/professional/enterprise rendered identical consoles. Deriving differences from backend seed data or hard-coded checks was explicitly rejected by the maintainer. Fixed with a frontend PLAN_FEATURES registry (feature key -> minimum plan), route/widget feature annotations owned by each module, shell filtering for menu/tabs/routes/widgets, an upgrade page for direct URLs, and a read-only plan matrix in the tenant create/edit dialog. The backend still treats plan as data (the pre-existing plan-to-quota mapping is untouched) and seeds no plan-specific console features. Backend role permissions remain the authorization boundary; the plan gate is UX-only.

C2 (P2): the code generator's external-datasource picker exposed every tenant's datasource rows and the manage button regardless of plan. Fixed by filtering the picker to the current datasource when the plan is below enterprise, disabling management, and labeling the locked state; the backend datasource permission stays required for enterprise tenants.

D1 (P3, fixed): after a tenant administrator opened a forbidden URL directly, the opened-tabs bar kept that tab for the session although the page itself rendered 403 and no tenant data loaded. Fixed by deriving both the tab bar and the command palette from selectAccessibleTabs, which applies the same plan-entitlement plus route-pagePermission predicate used for rendering; a browser probe on a free tenant now leaves only 工作台 after direct visits to /system/tenant (403) and /system/generator (upgrade page).

acceptanceCriteria: A tenant-scoped session never receives system.tenant, /system/menu, or /system/i18n in its navigation or management tree, and a direct URL renders the permission-denied page without loading tenant data.
The platform administrator still sees tenant, menu, and i18n management menus and can create tenants with a visible plan matrix.
A tenant login writes exactly one success row in the tenant's own login-log view, and failed/MFA attempts are attributed to the subject or challenge tenant; compat deployments keep rows at tenant 0.

Free hides the low-code group and both low-code routes show the upgrade page; basic exposes module management but not the generator; professional exposes the generator with a locked datasource picker; enterprise unlocks datasource management.
No plan-specific feature difference is implemented by backend seed data or hard-coded tenant initialization.

Backend -race suite (real MySQL + Redis), frontend unit tests, type-check, lint, contracts, build, and i18n parity pass; evidence records the exact commands, results, environment limits, and residual gaps.

doNotTouch: CI required checks and gate thresholds

implementationNotes: Platform-only classification is centralized in pkg/tenant/platform_scope.go and consumed by menu reads, provisioning, role assignment, and permission caching.
Provisioning strips platform-only bindings on both first run and re-provisioning; Bootstrap runs an idempotent repair for pre-fix tenants and never touches tenant_id 0.

Plan entitlements live only in frontend/src/core/entitlements/plans.ts. Modules declare feature keys; the shell filters menus, routes, and dashboard widgets; the backend receives no plan-derived configuration.
Login audit attribution uses the issued tenant claim on success and the subject's owning tenant on failure; compat keeps tenant 0 so rows remain readable by compat administrators.
The shared tenant session store is reset both on logout and at the Login.tsx login boundary, so re-login in the same tab cannot inherit the previous subject's plan or tenant viewpoint.
Unknown plan values normalize to free; unknown feature keys fail open; platform scope and compat bypass the plan gate.

Opened tabs and command-palette entries are derived through selectAccessibleTabs so a plan-locked or permission-forbidden path never persists as a tab, including tabs recorded before the tenant session resolved.
